# Cirvane v0.1.0: Recovery you can inspect

Cirvane's first developer release provides bounded, recovery-focused firmware that makes operational state, rejected work and rollback visible instead of hiding failure.

- Connect a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 to Wi-Fi through a guided, password-masked shell workflow.
- Install owner-signed updates from fixed GitHub Release origins over authenticated HTTPS, with bounded downloads and fail-closed verification.
- Recover automatically when a newly installed image is not explicitly confirmed healthy.
- Inspect bounded services, resources, messages, evidence records and update state through the local USB shell.

The supported installation target is the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5. Install the full flash image by following the [installation guide](https://kabudu.github.io/cirvane/#install). This firmware is powered by ESP-IDF and FreeRTOS; it is not the separate clean-sheet kernel research path.

Hardware Secure Boot, flash encryption and irreversible eFuse provisioning are not enabled. Energy use, independent penetration testing, formal verification, independent novelty review and clean-room reproduction remain deferred.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/kabudu/cirvane/blob/v0.1.0/CHANGELOG.md), [validation record](https://github.com/kabudu/cirvane/blob/v0.1.0/docs/VALIDATION.md) and [security policy](https://github.com/kabudu/cirvane/security/policy) for the exact evidence and limits.
